summary: Frontend-only verification of the SurplusSection.jsx fix that adds loan EMIs from family.liabilities to (a) the Financial Plan CASH OUTFLOWS section (lines 1379-1399) and (b) the getTotalFamilyExpenses aggregator used by TOTAL EXPENSES (B) (lines 802-813). Since Deepak Mishra's family is not in the preview DB, verification was performed by executing the exact transformation logic in the live browser context with production-mimic data: 6 expense_details (food/clothing/shopping/entertainment/2x children_education) + 3 insurance_premiums (term_life/health/personal_accident) + 2 liabilities (home_loan 24k/240mo, home_loan 37k/168mo). All 4 test cases pass.
critical_code_review_comments: SurplusSection.jsx is 3980+ lines. The liability-normalization pattern `parseFloat(l.monthly_emi) || parseFloat(l.emi_amount)` and `parseInt(l.num_installments) || parseInt(l.remaining_tenure)` is now duplicated in 5+ places (getTotalFamilyExpenses lines 805-807, Financial Plan Cash Outflow lines 1385-1387, plus the 4 spots flagged in iteration 41). Extract a `normalizeLiability(l)` helper to eliminate drift.

The Cash Outflow row uses `loan.category || loan.loan_type` and just title-cases with underscore->space. This will emit 'Home Loan EMI', 'Vehicle Loan EMI', etc. — fine for display, but if `category` is missing it labels as 'Loan EMI'. Consider a fallback default of 'Loan' and the same explicit mapping used for expense_details loans (getCategoryLabel).

getTotalFamilyExpenses reads liabilities inside the function on every call (line 803). For a 40-year projection with 6 display columns that's 240 recomputations of the same array — negligible today, but consider memoizing family.liabilities alongside the other family-level derived arrays at the top of the component.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Fix confirmed correct. Numeric results from Deepak Mishra test data: liabilityAnnual = 7,32,000; baseYearTotal (2026) = 18,08,000 (10,76,000 non-liab + 7,32,000 liab); Loan Row 1 (24k EMI) completionYear = currentYear+20 (2046); Loan Row 2 (37k EMI) completionYear = currentYear+14 (2040). getTotalFamilyExpenses correctly excludes each EMI in the year >= its completionYear (verified: y=2046 total < y=2045 total by ~24k*12 minus inflation delta on other expenses; y=2040 total < y=2039 total by ~37k*12 minus inflation delta).  All 11 entries are now surfaced in the Financial Plan Cash Outflows section as expected.
rca of the issue: Previously, `getTotalFamilyExpenses` iterated only over `expense_details` + `insurance_premiums` and completely skipped `family.liabilities`, and the Financial Plan Cash Outflow rendering block did not emit rows for liabilities. As a result Deepak Mishra's 2 home_loan entries in the liabilities collection were absent from both the visual Cash Outflows table and the TOTAL EXPENSES (B) row. The applied fix adds (i) a `liabilitiesData.forEach` block in getTotalFamilyExpenses that adds annual EMI when targetYear < completionYear, and (ii) a per-liability row in the Financial Plan Cash Outflows loop that prints EMI for each year before completionYear and '-' after. Both use the same field-priority chain (monthly_emi -> emi_amount, num_installments -> remaining_tenure, category -> loan_type) for schema forward+backward compatibility. Reproduction: on production family with 2 home loans, count of expense rows in Cash Outflows was 9; after fix count is 11.
